metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.topic: Genetics — Monohybrid Cross: Purebred Tall × Unknown
metadata.note: 7m: cross purebred tall (TT) × unknown; all offspring same phenotype. T=tall (dominant), t=short (recessive). If all offspring are tall, the unknown parent could be TT or Tt (or even tt — since TT×tt gives all Tt which are all tall). Most likely intended scenario: TT × Tt → all tall. Steps: define alleles(1m) + parent phenotypes(1m) + parent genotypes(1m) + gametes(1m) + Punnett square(2m) + offspring phenotype(1m). Accept TT×tt as alternative if student correctly identifies all offspring as Tt (all tall).

question.name: CSEC Bio Jan 2024 Q5e — Genetics Cross: Purebred Tall × Unknown
question.text:
In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over short (t).

A purebred tall plant was crossed with an unknown plant. ALL offspring from the cross had the same phenotype.

Draw a genetic diagram to show a possible cross that could produce this result. State the phenotype of the offspring. (7 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Possible crosses (purebred tall TT × unknown) where ALL offspring have same phenotype:

Option A: TT × TT → all TT (all tall)

TT
TTTTT
TTTTT

All offspring: TT (tall)

Option B: TT × Tt → 50% TT + 50% Tt (all tall)

TT
TTTTT
tTtTt

All offspring: tall (TT or Tt)

Option C: TT × tt → all Tt (all tall)

TT
tTtTt
tTtTt

All offspring: Tt (tall — T is dominant over t)

Key point: In all three cases, tall phenotype dominates. The most interesting case is TT × Tt (reveals heterozygous parent) or TT × tt (all offspring are heterozygous).

steps.label:
Alleles: T = tall (dominant) | t = short (recessive)
Purebred tall: TT
All offspring same phenotype → unknown can be TT, Tt, or tt (all give tall offspring when crossed with TT)
Define alleles and state parent phenotypes. (2 marks)
State parent genotypes and gametes produced. (2 marks)
Complete Punnett square and state offspring genotypes and phenotypes. (3 marks)

fields.label: What does T represent? _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: T is the dominant allele that codes for the tall phenotype.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: T represents the dominant allele for tall stem. In genetics, we use capital letters for dominant alleles and lowercase for recessive.

fields.label: Phenotype of the purebred parent = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The purebred tall parent has genotype TT and phenotype: tall.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Purebred tall means the plant has genotype TT (homozygous dominant). Its phenotype is tall.

fields.label: Genotype of the purebred tall parent = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Purebred = homozygous. Tall and purebred = TT (homozygous dominant).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Purebred (true-breeding) means homozygous. For the dominant tall trait: purebred tall = TT.

fields.label: Genotype of the unknown parent (a valid choice) = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Any of TT, Tt, or tt is a valid choice for the unknown parent — all give all-tall offspring when crossed with TT. Most commonly tested: Tt or tt.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: When the purebred tall parent (TT) crosses with an unknown: TT×TT → all TT (tall); TT×Tt → 50% TT + 50% Tt (all tall); TT×tt → all Tt (all tall). All three give 'same phenotype' offspring. Any of these is acceptable.

fields.label: Gametes from each parent (e.g. for TT × Tt): _____
fields.expected: TT parent: T and T; Tt parent: T and t
fields.diagnostic_hint: For TT × Tt: TT parent produces T and T gametes; Tt parent produces T and t gametes.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: During meiosis, alleles separate (Mendel's Law of Segregation). TT parent: both alleles are T, so all gametes carry T. Tt parent: one T allele and one t allele separate, so 50% of gametes carry T and 50% carry t.

options.TT parent: T and T; Tt parent: T and t: TT → T and T | Tt → T and t
options.TT parent: T and t; Tt parent: T and T: TT → T and t | Tt → T and T
options.Both parents produce only T and T: Both parents: T and T only
options.TT parent: T and T; tt parent: t and t: TT → T and T | tt → t and t

fields.label: Offspring genotypes from Punnett square (for chosen cross): _____
fields.expected: TT and Tt (for TT × Tt cross)
fields.diagnostic_hint: For TT × Tt: Punnett square gives TT, TT, Tt, Tt → 50% TT : 50% Tt. For TT × tt: all Tt. For TT × TT: all TT.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: For TT × Tt: cross T,T (from TT) with T,t (from Tt): T+T=TT; T+t=Tt; T+T=TT; T+t=Tt → 2TT : 2Tt = 1:1 ratio. For TT × tt: T+t, T+t, T+t, T+t → all Tt. For TT × TT: all TT.

fields.label: Phenotype of ALL offspring = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: In all valid crosses (TT×TT, TT×Tt, TT×tt), ALL offspring have at least one T allele → all offspring are tall (T is dominant).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: T is dominant over t. Any offspring with at least one T allele will be tall. Since the TT parent always contributes a T allele, all offspring will be tall regardless of the unknown parent's genotype.

fields.label: How was the Punnett square set up? (describe axis labels): _____
fields.expected: TT parent gametes (T,T) on one axis; chosen parent gametes on the other axis
fields.diagnostic_hint: Label the Punnett square rows and columns with the gametes from each parent, then fill in the boxes by combining alleles.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: A Punnett square has gametes from parent 1 along the top and gametes from parent 2 down the side. Each box is filled by combining the row and column alleles.

options.TT parent gametes (T,T) on one axis; cho: TT parent (T,T) on one axis; other parent gametes on other axis
options.TT parent gametes (T,t) on one axis; cho: TT parent (T,t) on one axis — incorrect gametes
options.Parent phenotypes on each axis instead o: Parent phenotypes (not gametes) on each axis
options.Both axes labelled with all possible gen: Both axes labelled with all genotypes
